_note: Combat parity fixture (01-08): four independent scenarios, each its own seed + forced encounter, so every outcome (win/lose/flee/parley) is deterministic and reachable in a small, fixed action count. `startCombat` is NOT in engine/actions.js's validated ACTION_TYPES (it is an internal function other rule domains call, not a player-facing action) -- test/parity/combat-parity.test.js special-cases it, calling engine/combat.js's startCombat directly (state/rng managed the same way applyAction does) and the prototype's `ctx.startCombat(wandering, forced)` directly, exactly mirroring the encounter the wandering-monster check or an encounter dot would eventually trigger. Every scenario's seed was found by a throwaway discovery script that simulated the engine directly against a forced encounter type until it produced the desired outcome (same method 01-05/01-07 used for chargen/movement fixture seeds), then cross-checked for prototype parity before being committed here.
